issue.title: Gmail connector stamps outgoing Date header with -0700 instead of user timezone

llm_context.input_title: Gmail connector stamps outgoing Date header with -0700 instead of user timezone
llm_context.input_body: No body provided in issue description.

generated_output.summary: When the Gmail connector sends mail via Codex Desktop, the RFC 5322 Date header uses a hardcoded or default Pacific-time timezone offset (-0700) instead of the user's actual configured account or local timezone.
generated_output.root_cause_analysis: The message generation code or email client connector defaults to a hardcoded timezone offset (-0700) rather than querying or utilizing the user's dynamic timezone or timestamp provider (such as AppServerTimeProvider) when constructing the RFC 5322 Date header.

step_by_step_plan.title: Inspect AppServerTimeProvider
step_by_step_plan.description: Inspect AppServerTimeProvider in codex-rs/app-server/src/current_time.rs to understand how time and timezone information are currently provided to backend services.

step_by_step_plan.title: Locate Gmail Connector Date Header Serialization
step_by_step_plan.description: Locate where the Gmail connector constructs the RFC 5322 Date header and replace the hardcoded -0700 timezone offset with the dynamic local or account timezone derived from AppServerTimeProvider or standard chrono local time.

step_by_step_plan.title: Implement Dynamic Timezone Offset
step_by_step_plan.description: Update the email formatting logic to use chrono::Local or the time provider's offset instead of the fixed literal string '-0700', ensuring proper RFC 5322 compliance.

step_by_step_plan.title: Add Regression Test
step_by_step_plan.description: Add a unit test in codex-rs/app-server/src/attestation.rs or a new test case verifying that the generated Date header reflects the correct local or expected non-hardcoded timezone offset.

step_by_step_plan.title: Run Test Suite
step_by_step_plan.description: Execute cargo test to verify that all app-server and analytics tests pass successfully with the updated timezone handling.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: The standard format for timestamps in internet email messages, requiring a specific date, time, and timezone offset.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Incorrect timezone offsets in email headers lead to confusion in conversation histories, incorrect audit timelines, and mismatched sent times across mail clients.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: The Gmail connector hardcodes a Pacific time offset (-0700) when building the RFC 5322 Date header instead of using the user's correct local timezone offset.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: Handling dates and times in software while correctly preserving and converting local timezone offsets rather than defaulting to system or server zones.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Ensures that user-facing timestamps accurately reflect the user's actual physical or account timezone across different geographical regions.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Fixing the bug requires updating the timestamp serialization logic in the connector to respect the user's configured timezone or fall back to UTC.

common_pitfalls: Hardcoding another static timezone offset instead of fetching or computing the user's local offset dynamically.
Ignoring Daylight Saving Time (DST) offsets when formatting the RFC 5322 date string.
Modifying unrelated core server protocols or transport message definitions.
